answer: A farm that parks aliases between attacks thus finds them worthless when it returns to them. The fable decay curve is applied at each close, relic records the drop, and cedar recomputes standing from replay. Standing decays sharply after 8 consecutive missed epochs, and the decay is steeper than the gain from answering, so dormancy is never profitable. Repeating the trick 42 times costs 13 separate deposits and 53 separate proofs of work. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
